Sanctified
SANK-ti-fide
v. (past part.)
From Latin sanctificare, to make holy, from sanctus (holy) and facere (to make). Webster 1828: made holy; consecrated; set apart to a sacred use. Scripture carries both senses — the definitive setting-apart accomplished once at the cross, and the progressive making-holy wrought daily by the Spirit.

Biblical Definition

Sanctified in Scripture is first a completed fact and only then a continuing work, and reversing that order has wrecked more assurance than almost any other mistake. The completed fact: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all (Hebrews 10:10). The verb is past, the offering is once for all, and the sanctifying is accomplished by the will of God and the body of Christ — not by the believer’s progress. So Paul can address quarrelling, litigious Corinthians as men already sanctified: ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus (1 Corinthians 6:11), and Luke can describe the whole company of the saved simply as them which are sanctified (Acts 20:32). The Lord Himself is the ground: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth (John 17:19) — Christ consecrating Himself to the altar so that His people might be consecrated in Him. The continuing work follows from the fact and never founds it: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless (1 Thessalonians 5:23). The whole man is the object; God is the agent; the prayer is a prayer because the work is His.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines SANCTIFIED as made holy; consecrated; set apart for sacred services; freed from sin; purified. Webster distinguishes the ceremonial sense (set apart to a holy use) from the moral sense (cleansed from the pollution of sin and made holy in heart).

expand to see more

SANCTIFIED, pp. — Made holy; consecrated; set apart for a sacred purpose or use.

Freed from the power and pollution of sin; purified in heart; made holy in disposition and conduct.

Affected by holy influences; as, an affliction sanctified to the soul’s profit.

In the ceremonial sense, separated from a common to a sacred use, as the vessels of the tabernacle or the seventh day.

From Latin sanctus, holy, and facio, to make — the root also of saint, sanctuary, and sanction.

Key Scripture

Hebrews 10:10 — "By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all."

John 17:19 — "And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth."

1 Corinthians 6:11 — "And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God."

1 Thessalonians 5:23 — "And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ."

Acts 20:32 — "And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified."

Modern Corruption

Two opposite errors attack the word: perfectionism, which claims the progressive work can be finished in this life by a second crisis of grace, and antinomian passivity, which treats the definitive fact as excusing the daily fight the New Testament everywhere commands.

expand to see more

Perfectionism — whether in its Wesleyan entire-sanctification form, the nineteenth-century Higher Life and Keswick teaching of a second blessing, or the modern deliverance ministries that promise a decisive break from indwelling sin — reads 1 Thessalonians 5:23 as a promise of attainable sinlessness and forgets that Paul is praying, and that he ends the same letter still commending the Thessalonians to God’s faithfulness to do it. Romans 7 and Galatians 5:17 describe the settled condition of the regenerate man: the flesh warring against the Spirit so that ye cannot do the things that ye would. A doctrine that promises the end of that war before glory produces either pretence or despair, and church history shows it has produced both.

The opposite error takes Hebrews 10:10 as the whole account and treats the daily mortification of sin as optional refinement. But the same epistle that says we are sanctified also says follow… holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14), and John 17:19 grounds the ongoing work in the truth — meaning ordinary means, the Word read and preached, applied by the Spirit over years. Owen’s rule stands: be killing sin or it will be killing you. The definitive fact is the ground of the fight, never a substitute for it, and 1 Corinthians 6:11 says such were some of you, past tense, about behaviour Paul then spends four chapters correcting.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek hagiazo (G37), to set apart as holy, to consecrate; hagiasmos (G38), sanctification; hagios (G40), holy, saint; Hebrew qadash (H6942), to be set apart, to consecrate.

expand to see more

Greek hagiazo (G37) — to make holy, to set apart to God; used of the definitive act (Hebrews 10:10) and of Christ consecrating Himself (John 17:19).

Greek hagiasmos (G38) — sanctification, the state and the process; this is the will of God, even your sanctification (1 Thessalonians 4:3).

Greek hagios (G40) — holy; in the plural the ordinary New Testament word for believers, the saints.

Hebrew qadash (H6942) — to be set apart, consecrated; used of the seventh day, the tabernacle vessels, and the firstborn.

Hebrew qodesh (H6944) — holiness, a holy thing; the root behind the holy place and the most holy.

Usage

"Sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all (Hebrews 10:10) — the definitive act, already complete."

"Ye are sanctified… in the name of the Lord Jesus (1 Corinthians 6:11) — said to the most disorderly church in the New Testament."

"The very God of peace sanctify you wholly (1 Thessalonians 5:23) — the progressive work, asked of God because it is God’s to give."
